hero.lede: Specs live in GitHub and Confluence, but their reviews die in PR threads and meeting chat. Kedge turns any source into one readable review page: discussion anchored to the text, approvals pinned to versions, and AI on tap to strengthen the doc.

surface.heading: Comments that keep their place
surface.body: A real review in Kedge: the doc rendered for reading, threads pinned to the exact sentences they question, approvals pinned to the version they saw. Ship a new version and the discussion re-anchors instead of washing away.
surface.screenshotAlt: A spec rendered in Kedge, with comment threads anchored to sentences in the text and version-pinned approve and re-sync actions

how.heading: Review where the doc is readable, not where it’s stored
how.body: Three steps from a URL to a running review. No migration, no new home for your docs, and reviewers never need accounts.

import.title: Import from anywhere
import.body: A GitHub file, a whole repo directory, a raw URL, an upload. Diagrams render, broken markup never crashes the page, and a share link exists in seconds.

discuss.title: Discuss on the text itself
discuss.body: Select a sentence, start a thread. Propose the fix as a suggested edit the author accepts in one click. Reviewers join by magic link, no accounts to herd.

resync.title: Ship a new version, keep the review
resync.body: Re-sync pulls the latest doc and every comment finds its place again: exact match first, fuzzy match second, the orphan tray as the safety net. Approvals show exactly which version they vouch for.

agents.heading: Your next reviewer might not be human
agents.body1: Kedge’s MCP server makes AI agents first-class reviewers. They read the rendered doc, anchor comments to real passages, and wear a badge that says exactly what they are. Nothing an agent writes posts without a human confirming it.
agents.body2: Then close the loop: fold the review into an AI digest, hand your coding agent the improve-prompt, re-sync the revised doc, and the whole discussion is still there.

workspace.heading: Point it at your docs/ folder and every spec arrives review-ready
workspace.body: A project tracks a repo, a branch, and a path pattern. Kedge previews the matches, bulk-imports them, and a re-scan after each push imports new files, re-syncs changed ones, and flags deletions. It never deletes anything itself.

points.status: Live import status on every doc, retry inline
points.glance: Lifecycle, open threads, and sync state at a glance
points.unfiled: An Unfiled bucket, so nothing needs a home first

roadmap.heading: Live today, charted next
roadmap.intro: Six releases in July, each one demoed on Kedge’s own docs the week it landed. The chart from here:

live.import: Import from GitHub, raw URLs, uploads, private repos
live.threads: Anchored threads and one-click suggested edits
live.versions: Versions, diffs, and approvals that go visibly stale
live.projects: Workspace projects and tracked repos with re-scan

charted.ai: AI reviewers and digests over MCP, in development now
charted.inbox: A review inbox: mentions, digests, what needs you
charted.sync: GitHub App and Confluence sync: push once, it re-syncs itself
charted.selfhost: Self-host GA: one command, full parity, AGPL-3.0

roadmap.closer: Both editions launch together: the SaaS for anyone with a URL, the compose file for teams whose specs stay home.

selfHost.heading: Your specs never have to leave home
selfHost.body: The open-source edition is the entire product: anchoring, approvals, the MCP server, all of it. AGPL-3.0, full parity with the SaaS, one compose file.

terminal.frontDoor: sign in is the front door

cta.body: Leave your email to open a workspace for your team’s specs. Nothing to install, no credit card, and the demo works before you decide.
